meeting.title: Spokane Chiefs <> Salesforce/Mulesoft: Pacolon integration financial discussion

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Yes, it's good.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: How's the weather over there? Is it finally spring-summer weather?

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: It's good today, but tomorrow looks gloomy. Possibility of rain, so [Laughter] have to see how it goes. But yeah, it's better than the weight of so sometime to kind of enjoy.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Four? Yeah, I think I probably told you this, I'm from Maine, so used to the winters and... Nothing like the spring thaw out. Hey, Brandon, how are you doing?

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Hey.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Great. How are you doing? Sorry for starting a little late.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: No worries. All right, any questions on your end? Otherwise happy to kind of jump in what I got and kind of get your thoughts on what I got approved from the pricing side of things.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
No real questions. We just kind of laid it all out there for the leadership and answered any questions that they had. It seemed like they were receptive. But again, since we have two teams in the area trying to become more united front, it seemed like they were really interested as well. Just kind of see the cost on their end to see if it kind of fits in their budget. Them being part of minor league baseball and major league baseball kind of umbrella, they do have a different ticketing platform and they have different kind of intricacies.
So they know that's need a different kind of integration. And so they're kind of looking into their own budget that way, but at least trying to see if there is some sort of discount for doing the combined teams like that.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Yeah. That's something that I definitely got approved. Then I guess Kailash from your side too. It sounds like on the baseball side of things, we maybe looking around in October timeline to start scoping out what anything would look like over there.
That is that, right? Okay, cool. Perfect, so let me pull up what I got here. Okay, so this is what we were talking about last time, just for the Chiefs. The $19,500, right? As you guys were asking, like, "Hey, you know, the discounting percentage on the old SKUs versus the new SKUs."
Why is the one on the new SKUs so much lower? I'd been told we couldn't go below 20% discount on the new Mulesoft SKUs, so I was a little bit surprised. Honestly, the total that I got, verbal confirmation we could offer should you guys do both, is about 35% off list, right?
It's a $15,500 list priced at $19,500 each. So $3,1000 for the total for both. So the increase of getting both versus just the Chiefs is $11,500. Then the other thing that I was able to get again, verbal approval on is breaking these out into quarterly payments. Hopefully, better aligned with timelines and annual budget resets. As Michelle mentioned on our last call too, we can get a little bit creative with structuring start dates to again align better with that. The one caveat with that is we would just need both order forms signed in June to honor those couple of terms.
This is what we were... David and I got approved for. You all are here, so I wanted to pause. Let you guys take it in and feel free to ask any questions that you have.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Would we have...? Would it be one overarching contract or would there be two separate contracts? The Chiefs and the Indians. Would we sign two separate ones or would it just be one?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
So it... My understanding is it would be two separate just because you have two separate instances in software systems. And just from a governance side of things, it's just easier to do it that way. But
that allows us to change start dates a little bit too, right? If we want the Chiefs to kick off on, like, July 15th and maybe, you know, we want to see what we can do on the Indian side of things.
Like it would. It would let us play with that, too.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text:
Cool. Yeah, I know. We'll have to present it to the Indians first. Brandon and I had a meeting with them earlier today. We kicked the door open about that we're going to have an internal meeting and get going there.
So we do have the wheel spinning there. Hopefully, we can have them make a decision real soon from the chief side. We're pretty sure we're ready to go. We've built it into our budget and we proposed that, and they basically said yes.
So I think from our standpoint, we just really need to put a little pressure on the Indians to make a decision quickly. But otherwise, it seems like our trains are heading down the tracks correctly from the chief side.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay. CO so I guess what can we do from our side to help give you guys the resources to kind of present everything to the Indians team? I can share this slide over. Is there anything else we can do to help on that side of things.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text:
I feel like we have a lot of the previous meetings that we've done, and we can share that with them. So I think we're good on that. I think for them, they're trying to figure out what they can pull out of tickets.com that it's owned by Mob.
So it's a little bit different. So I think they're just looking more into the operational side of how and what that would work for them. So if we do think of anything, we'll definitely reach out for extra material.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Okay. And that's something too on our end all again to just again. I'm sure ticketing.com as some sort of API documentation or something out there is that's something that Kailash and I can check into a you know, maybe at least share some insights on to what information can you pull? Are you able to pull it all?
You know, the this the same sort of stuff that we did for y'all.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text:
Yeah, that'd be perfect. And then I do know they have like another software that it's innately linked to tickets.com. It's called Stellar ago. And that they were thinking like instead of maybe doing Tickets dot com that they would, if possible, have you guys linked Stellar all go to that instead, one would just kind of filter things a little bit more.
And so it may be cleaner for them, but yeah, I think either if we presented those to either one of them, they'd be happy to hear.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay, cool. Yeah, we can look into that if one or the other is going to be materially easier to stand up. We're happy to share any guidance from our end. But that totally tracks. I'm assuming it's going to be the same kind of use case here, right? Just so we know what we're looking for.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Exactly.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Perfect. Then I think David has a call with Nick over on the Indian team later today, just for a brief check-in. Anything around this project that you want us to check in on or anything that we should ask?

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text:
I know Nick has a... We have a technology committee, and that is tomorrow, Thursday. So I know he's going to hear more about it on Thursday. He wasn't in the earlier meeting today, so I don't know if he knows, but I think it's always good to bring something up that we're exploring the connections and how to do those APIs.
If Nick knows that, he may be like, "Well, I've been thinking about this. And then, that could potentially lead into the conversation on saving with dual pricing and doing that. But yeah, I'm not sure exactly how up to speed he is on what we talked about today.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: But yeah.

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: DR.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Sure, yeah, I mean, easy enough. It's the same thing. We just want to be able to talk through and show how this will work once it's stood up so that you're not just making decisions based on a hope and a prayer here.
So totally fine. I guess from our end, we'll send all this information over to you. I'll start poking around to see which of those two systems might be easier to sync with. Would it make sense for us all to connect at the end of this week or early next week just to make sure we're keeping this thing moving along? Or what would be best for us?

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: We could probably get a Friday because, yeah, if we target Friday... If I have to be early, let's look at Monday next week.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay. Is morning or afternoon typically better?

content.speaker: Speaker 4
content.text: Afternoons are pretty good.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Cool. It looks like anytime between twelve and two in the afternoon works on our end.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: That it worked anytime between them with just two.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: So...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Yeah, perfectly and everything. And then if you could send me over, kind of the full breakout with the users, the premier success plan and everything just so we can kind of see the difference between the rate with the Indians included and then without just we can bring that to leadership just can kind of show the differences.
And what you guys were able to do for us, they probably really appreciate that.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Absolutely. Yeah. I'll put together a couple more slides that spell it out a little more clearly there, and then if it's still missing anything, just let me know. Happy to make edits. Really want to make sure it's useful and understandable, specifically for those folks who maybe haven't been on any of these calls.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Perfect.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Awesome, guys. We will get working on that. Unless anyone else has any other questions, I'll send the new meeting invite out, and then we'll get to work and start sharing stuff over as we start tracking down answers. Rubert.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Appreciate.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: It. Okay, thank you, thank.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: You.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Bye.
